context.objective: Document how we carry out Capital Call & Distribution Event Execution, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It starts when a client tells us, or we identify, a need to move capital: a line of credit repayment, investment funding, a management fee, operating expenses, portfolio company proceeds or an ad hoc request. Let me walk the whole thing end to end. Step 1, the assigned preparer (CAP Activity Team or Fund Team, it depends on the event and client) opens the event: classifies it as a capital call, distribution or combined net event, records driver, entity, amount and expected cash dates, and names the preparer and second reviewer. Step 2, the preparer builds the event calendar from the LPA notice rule (business or calendar days) and checks bank holidays and payment cut-offs; if a requested date cannot meet the notice rule or cut-off we escalate. Step 3, the preparer assembles the data pack and marks every input final, estimated or pending. Step 4, the preparer copies the prior locked Excel event file forward, pulls beginning balances from the power report, trial balance and partner capital files and ties them to the prior deliverable; an unexplained difference is escalated to the reviewer and client before calculations are finalized. Step 5, preparer with reviewer and client freezes the methodology; if LPA treatment is ambiguous we pause and get written client or legal direction. Step 6, population gate: preparer lists every investor, reviewer checks independently; any unconfirmed change stays excluded until written client direction. Step 7, preparer runs the allocations in Excel and fills the summary allocation tab; investor totals must equal fund totals apart from documented rounding. Step 8, preparer reconciles to partner capital, GP unfunded and trial balance, reviewer verifies; any unexplained difference pauses client submission. Step 9, the second reviewer does the internal review; comments go back to the preparer for correction, otherwise sign-off. Step 10, preparer sends the package to the client; feedback means we revise and repeat affected checks; on final written approval we lock the file. No posting or release before that. Step 11, preparer merges notices from the summary tab into the Word template, converts to PDF, and the reviewer compares each notice to the locked allocation in e-check; failures are regenerated, never patched. Step 12, Fund Team or preparer prepares journal entries, routes them through accounting review and posts in the GL (Allvue or Entrilia); for cash outflows Treasury initiates payment after bank detail controls. Step 13, Investor Services splits notices, uploads to the investor portal and releases the email campaign, holding release on any mapping or contact discrepancy. Step 14, closeout: for a call we hand the receivable baseline to receipt tracking; for a distribution we confirm wires settled; update historical records, complete client deliverables and retain the final package.
When GPFS identifies a need internally, what typically brings it to the team's attention?

I do not know. The overall process owner and the internal approver have not been confirmed, and ownership between the CAP Activity Team and the Fund Team is not standardized. What I can say is that the preparing team and a second reviewer from the assigned operating team must be named when the event opens, the second reviewer must sign off before anything goes to the client, and the client approves the final event amounts and notices. The exact role title of the second reviewer is also not confirmed.
What inputs and allocation steps does the preparer use in Excel to get from the approved methodology to each investor’s amount?

Money moves on this work, so investors could be asked to fund the wrong amounts by a due date or be paid the wrong proceeds. The specific failures we guard against are: the event run for the wrong investor population, which means the event has failed even if the math is right; a notice that does not agree with the locked allocation; a missed manual notice step that discloses information to the wrong party or releases inconsistent notices; a due date that breaks the LPA notice rule or lands on a bank holiday or past a cut-off so it cannot be executed; and a posted GL entry that does not equal the locked totals. If an error or a late client change is found after posting, the entry has to be reversed and reposted through the controlled accounting workflow, and the affected review, notice and approval steps are repeated. Errors also flow downstream into receipt tracking for calls, distribution economics and Treasury execution.
How does the frozen methodology translate into the investor-level calculations in the Excel event file?

I cannot give you a measured breakdown of where the time goes, nobody has estimated that. What I can say: setup and inputs are manual and depend on client instructions. Allocation rules and percentages live in Excel, and every event starts by copying the prior workbook forward and tying beginning balances to the prior deliverable; the workbook can carry manual entries, plugs, manual rounding, hidden tabs, broken links and outdated settings that have to be sourced or cleaned up. Historical proceeds, tax details and special rules can be spread across several workpapers. Rework mainly comes from repeated client changes, which make version control harder, and from changes after posting, which force a reversal and repost with renewed approvals. Investor Services also has to split notices manually and coordinate the email campaign. As a rough example only, a basic capital call takes a couple of hours, while a complex distribution with holdbacks, tranches, waterfall or tax coordination can take a couple of days or longer.
About how many capital-call or distribution events does the team typically handle in a month or year?

Several things. For One Rock we complete a Cobalt upload within two days of a capital event, at closeout. GP vehicles have their own population, waiver, commitment and carry rules. Deal-by-deal or tranche-based funds keep separate allocation history per investment or tranche. For net events we keep the call and distribution components separate even when the investor sees one net amount. Notice timing varies by fund: some LPAs use business days, some calendar days, and they are not interchangeable. Where the governing documents are silent on an allocation treatment, we only use a written, current client-approved methodology for that specific fund. Clients can also elect the narrative, notice date, presentation, net-event display or recipient population, and that is recorded in the event brief. The GL platform and journal entry approval route differ by entity, Allvue or Entrilia, but which entity uses which is not confirmed. And when we also service the management company, invoice information comes from that team as well as the Fund Team. Nothing differs by country or currency that I know of.
What determines whether the CAP Activity Team or Fund Team prepares an event?

open_questions: S4 (Carry forward and tie balances) uses “locked event file”, which S10 (Obtain client approval) produces, but no route leads from S10 to S4. What connects them?
Does any incoming route start S5 (Freeze methodology), or must all prerequisites finish?
Does any incoming route start S11 (Generate notices), or must all prerequisites finish?
Does any incoming route start S16 (Close out event), or must all prerequisites finish?
How is an internally identified need detected and received, and what are the normal cadence and event deadlines?
Who is accountable overall and who is the internal approver? How is work assigned between the CAP Activity Team and Fund Team?
What inputs and Excel calculation sequence produce each investor amount, including dates, rounding, overrides and corrections? Who owns the workbook logic?
What does each reviewer check, what evidence is retained and where, and which controls are procedural or system-enforced?
Who checks posted GL entries against locked totals, how is the check performed, and where does it sit relative to closeout?
When and in what form does the client approve notices, given that PDF notice generation follows final written approval and file lock?
Who receives calendar escalations, how are discrepancies resolved, and where do paused or corrected items return?
After internal review corrections or client feedback, how are the required sign-off and subsequent handoffs completed?
How are bank details controlled, and how are mapping or contact discrepancies resolved before release?
After a post-posting error or late change, in what order are reversal, reposting and affected reviews, notices and approvals completed?
Which entity types and clients does this account cover? For the reported variants, what changes in effort, charging or removal constraints where relevant?
Is this the participant's normal route or general GPFS practice, and what is the basis? Independent corroboration remains UNKNOWN.
Which entity uses each GL platform and approval route? What is the authoritative record for each material result, and where are files and evidence stored?
Who interprets conflicting rules, where is the interpretation recorded, and what are the sources of GP vehicle and client-specific rules?
Who performs closeout and the One Rock upload, where is the final package retained, and who uses the client deliverables?
What are usual event volumes, peaks and exception frequency? A measured effort breakdown is unavailable.
Are procedures, checklists, examples or training materials available for review? The reported LPA, template and prior files have not been reviewed.
What other exceptions or returns occur, if any?
